sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two levels of drawing down through the work of many correspond to the two levels of the thirteen attributes.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that the two matters in the drawing down that comes through the work
(prayer or study of Torah)
of many,
that the drawing down is without gradation
(above the chain of descent),
and that through their work there is also drawn from a place where an arousal from below cannot
(even an arousal from below of many)
arouse there,
corresponds to the two levels mentioned above.
For in the level of thirteen,
where the one is drawn into the twelve,
since twelve is a boundary,
the drawing down from there is through an arousal from below.
But through the one that is drawn into the twelve,
the drawing down is without gradation
(analogous to "I toiled and I found").
And in the level of thirteen,
where the twelve are included in the one and all thirteen are in the thirty-three,
the drawing down from there is analogous to an arousal from above that comes from its own essence.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the concepts of twelve and thirteen to the liberation festival of 12-13 Tammuz, explaining the nature of the redemption.

translations.translation: And one can connect this with the festival of liberation, 12-13 Tammuz,
that on 12 Tammuz
[the birthday of the one who was liberated]
they informed him that an order for his release had arrived,
and the actual release was on 13 Tammuz43.
And it can be said,
that this, that on the twelfth
(of Tammuz)
they informed him about the release,
is the matter of twelve, as the one is drawn into it44.
And since twelve, as it is in its place,
even when the one is drawn into it,
is a boundary,
therefore on the twelfth it was still before the actual redemption.
For the matter of redemption is above measure and limitation
[and particularly according to what is explained in the letter of the one who was liberated
[that came as an introduction to the maamar beginning "Ten who sit"]
that the Holy One, blessed be He, redeemed not only him but also all of Israel,
including even those who are called by the name Israel
(only45)
are designated46.
And to add,
that in this are also included the generations that follow,
for the redemption of 12-13 Tammuz is a continuous action,
that draws redemption for all of Israel throughout all the generations,
redemption regarding their study of Torah and fulfillment of mitzvos, and also redemption regarding their physical matters,
children, life, and sustenance,
that they should all be "at ease,"
above measure and limitation.
And moreover,
that it
(the redemption of 12-13 Tammuz)
is also an introduction and preparation for the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach47,
when there will be the true matter of being above measure and limitation],
and the actual redemption was on the thirteenth, which numerically equals one,
when the twelve are elevated into the one,
above limitation.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses that although Torah is a drawing down from above, it still requires work and effort, with two aspects of that effort.

translations.translation: And the maamar continues33,
that although Torah is a drawing down from above to below, nevertheless even in Torah there must be work and toil,
and there are two matters in this.
That in order for the study of Torah to be proper, it is through
[the introduction of48]
the work of prayer,
for "anyone who says, 'I have nothing but Torah,' does not even have Torah"49.
And also, the study of Torah itself must be with work and toil.
And in this there are two matters.
The toil in understanding the Torah,
"I toiled and I found."
And the toil in Torah to change one's nature and habit,
as the Sages said50,
"One who reviews his chapter one hundred times is not comparable to one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times"51,
for then specifically is he called a servant of God.
